The company closed in 2021. The freelance visa is a residence permit for self-employed immigrants. With a freelance visa, you can… Live anywhere in Germany Start a business or become a freelancer Bring your family to Germany [§ 29 AufenthG] Visit other Schengen countries without a visa Become a permanent resident after 3 to 5 years [§ 21 Abs. 4 AufenthG] Become a citizen after 5 years This guide explains how to apply for a freelance visa in Berlin or in your home country. The artist visa and the language teacher visa are the same thing as the freelance visa. The application process is the same.

If you are not a citizen of the EU, EEA or Switzerland, you need a residence permit to live in Germany. The freelance visa is a type of residence permit. If you are a permanent resident, you don’t need a freelance visa. You can already be self-employed. Who needs a residence permit?

title: Two types of freelance visa
text: There are two types of freelance visa, because there are two types of self-employed people: Freelancers ( Freiberufler) Artists, teachers, scientists, engineers, software developers and other professionals with special qualifications. If you sell professional services, you might be a freelancer. Delivery drivers, influencers, website operators and commercial photographers are not freelancers. [§ 18 Abs. 1 EStG (the Berlin Ausländerbehörde uses this definition of a Freiberufler), VAB A21.5 (October 2025), Accountable.de (2025), Accountable.de (2025)] Tradespeople ( Selbständiger or Gewerbetreibender) If you are not a Freiberufler, you are Selbständig. If you sell products or apps, or if you are a co-founder, you are usually Selbständig. [§ 21 AufenthG, § 18 EStG, 2 K 7356/18] The difference is important, because they have different requirements. For example, tradespeople need German clients, but freelancers don’t. The required documents are also different. Are you a Freiberufler or a Selbständiger?

To get a freelance visa, you need… Enough income In Berlin, your net income must be more than your rent + your health insurance + € 563 per month. If you support children or a spouse, you need a higher income. See the cost of living in Berlin. Self-employed work You must be self-employed. You can’t be an employee with social benefits. Fake self-employment is not allowed. If you only have one client, you might not get a freelance visa. Permission to do this job You must have all the permits and special qualifications needed for the job. For example, doctors, engineers and lawyers need special qualifications. – Find the requirements for your profession If you are over 45 years old, and you are not a citizen of the Dominican Republic, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines or Sri Lanka, you must have… [Berlin.de, Berlin.de, § 21 Abs. 2 and 3 AufenthG, VAB 21.2] A private retirement pension Your pension must guarantee € 1,612.53 per month for at least 12 years after you turn 67 years old. or a public pension You need a guaranteed public pension in Germany, Australia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Chile, India, Israel, Japan, Canada, Kosovo, Morocco, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, South Korea, Tunisia, Turkey or the United States. If you made 5 years of public pension payments in Germany, you have a guaranteed public pension. or € 232,204 in business assets If you are self-employed, but not a freelancer, you also need… A local economic interest If you are Selbständig, you must have clients in Germany, or hire German employees. [§ 21 Abs. 1 AufenthG, § 21 Abs. 5 AufenthG, Berlin.de, Sebastian Hoffmann (August 2023), Sebastian Hoffmann (December 2022), Sebastian Hoffmann (January 2023), exception (2023), exception (2021), Mirko Vorreuter (October 2025)] If you only have clients in other countries, you won’t get the freelance visa. If you are a Freiberufler, you don’t need German clients. You do not need to speak German to get a freelance visa. You do not need a degree or relevant education, except if your profession requires it. For example, you need a law degree to be a lawyer, but you don’t need a degree to be a freelance photographer. If you can’t get a freelance visa, there are other residence permits to start a business in Germany. For example, you might qualify for permanent residence. Freelance visa alternatives

You can apply for a freelance visa before or after you move to Germany. To apply after moving to Germany, you must… Come to Germany Apply for a freelance visa at your local Ausländerbehörde. If you don’t live in Berlin, find your local Ausländerbehörde and follow their instructions. Get your freelance visa Start your business You can apply in Germany if… You are a citizen of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco or San Marino [§ 41 AufenthV, Berlin.de] or you already have a German residence permit, and you want to change it or renew it or you have an EU Permanent Residence in another country or you have an opportunity card or you have a job seeker visa or you have a National Visa for self-employment that you must convert to a freelance visa If you can’t apply in Germany, you must apply in your home country. Your current residence permit might allow self-employment. If not, you must wait 7 weeks to 6 months for your freelance visa before you start working. It might be cheaper and safer if you apply in your home country, then come to Germany when you have permission to start your business. If you need help, an immigration lawyer or a relocation consultant can take care of everything. It costs € 500 to € 2,000. It’s a tax-deductible expense.

title: 1. Come to Germany
text: Come to Germany and prepare your freelance visa application. If you have a National Visa or residence permit Your current visa or residence permit might allow self-employment. If it expires after you applied for the freelance visa, you don’t need to leave Germany. It stays valid until you get your freelance visa. If you are a citizen of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco or San Marino You can come to Germany without a visa. You can stay 90 days in Germany without a residence permit. You can look for clients, and apply for the freelance visa in Germany. [§ 41 AufenthV, Berlin.de] You can’t start working before you get your freelance visa. Some people do it anyway. If you have an opportunity card You can come to Germany, then convert your opportunity card into a freelance visa. You can’t be self-employed with an opportunity card; you must wait for your freelance visa. If you have a Schengen visa Schengen visas are for tourism, not immigration. Usually, if you enter Germany with a Schengen visa, you can’t apply for a freelance visa in Germany. Your application will be rejected. You must apply in your home country. [Auswärtiges Amt, § 3 AufenthG, einwanderer.net. Exceptions in § 5 Abs. 2 S. 1 AufenthG] If these options don’t apply to you, you must apply for the freelance visa in your home country.

title: 2. Prepare your application
text: Before you apply for the freelance visa… Find a place to live It’s really hard to find your first apartment. It’s much harder for freelancers. Start looking as soon as you can. Your only options might be a WG or a furnished apartment. You must be allowed to register your address. Your landlord must give you a tenancy confirmation. If you can’t get a tenancy confirmation, you might not get a freelance visa. Your rent must be affordable. In Berlin, your income must be more than your rent + your health insurance + € 563 per month before taxes. Your apartment must be big enough. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child. You must be allowed to register your address. Your landlord must give you a tenancy confirmation. If you can’t get a tenancy confirmation, you might not get a freelance visa. Your rent must be affordable. In Berlin, your income must be more than your rent + your health insurance + € 563 per month before taxes. Your apartment must be big enough. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child. Get health insurance You need valid health insurance. Ask my insurance expert to help you choose the correct health insurance. Don’t choose insurance yourself; it’s a really bad idea. Many applications get rejected because people have the wrong health insurance. Prepare the required documents This takes a few weeks. Start as soon as you can. If you bring your family to Germany, you can apply for their family reunion visa at the same time. You must prepare their documents too. While you wait for an Ausländerbehörde appointment, you should also… Register your address ( Anmeldung) The Anmeldung is very important. When you register your address, you get a tax ID and a registration certificate. If you don’t do your Anmeldung, they might reject your application. Open a bank account You need it to pay your rent, pay your application fee, and get paid by your clients. You should open a separate bank account for your business. You can choose a bank from any EU country.

title: 3. Apply for the freelance visa
text: You must apply for the freelance visa online. You do not need an Ausländerbehörde appointment. Apply for the Freelance visa It costs € 100. It’s cheaper for Turkish citizens. You can pay with Visa, Mastercard or PayPal. You can’t pay with cash or Girocard. The fee is tax-deductible, so keep the receipt. If you have too many documents, merge them or make them smaller. After you pay and send your application, you can download a PDF. This is your proof of application. Save it for later.

title: 4. Wait
text: The Ausländerbehörde will process your application. It takes 7 weeks to 6 months. You must wait for their response. There is no way to track your application. If you wait more than 3 months, you can sue the Ausländerbehörde. While you wait, your current National Visa or residence permit might expire. It’s extended until the Ausländerbehörde processes your application. [§ 81 Abs. 5 AufenthG] If your visa or residence permit expires If your current permit allows self-employment, you can start your business already. If not, you must wait for your freelance visa. What happens while you wait

title: 5. Go to your appointment
text: A few months later, the Ausländerbehörde will email you an appointment date. If you get an appointment, you are almost guaranteed to get your freelance visa. Follow the instructions in the email. You might need to send extra documents, or bring them to your appointment. What happens during your appointment If your freelance visa is approved, you will get a second appointment to pick up your plastic residence card. While you wait, you can start freelancing. You will get a document that confirms this.

title: 6. Get your freelance visa
text: Go to your second Ausländerbehörde appointment and pick up your freelance visa. Your new freelance visa is valid for up to 3 years. [§ 21 Abs. 4 AufenthG, VAB 21.4] You might get a shorter freelance visa if they are not sure that your business will work. If you had a residence permit for over 3 years, you might get an “unrestricted” residence permit. It allows any kind of employment or self-employment. Check your new Zusatzblatt to see what you can do. How to pick up your freelance visa Tell us how long it took to apply for a residence permit in Berlin. This tool requires JavaScript to work.

section: How to apply in your country
text: You can also apply for a freelance visa in your country, then move to Germany. This is cheaper and safer, because you can start working as soon as you arrive in Germany. You don’t need to wait in Germany without an income. How to apply in your country You can also get an opportunity card, move to Germany, then convert it into a freelance visa. You can’t be self-employed with an opportunity card; you must wait for your freelance visa.

These are the required documents in Berlin. If you apply elsewhere, they require different documents. Check the website of the Ausländerbehörde, embassy or consulate where you apply. – Find your embassy or consulate Your documents must convince the Ausländerbehörde that your business will work, and that you will make enough money to support yourself. When you send your application, use PDF files or photos. Don’t use word documents or other file formats. If you have too many documents, merge them or make them smaller. You can also mail your documents, but it’s not better or faster. When you go to your appointment, bring the documents that they ask for in your appointment confirmation. Put dates on all your documents. Print everything on A4 paper. Do not staple the pages together. Some case workers also ask for documents that you already sent. It’s safer if you bring everything you have, including documents that you already sent.

title: Required documents for everyone
text: Passport Include a colour scan of your passport in your application. When you go to your appointment, bring your original passport. You get it back during the appointment; they do not keep it. Application form ( Antrag auf Erteilung eines Aufenthaltstitels) If this is your first residence permit application, fill this form. Download the form here or on Berlin.de. Proof of health insurance You need valid health insurance. Ask my insurance expert to help you choose health insurance for your work visa. Health insurance card Show both sides of the card. or proof of public health insurance Get a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB V from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. or proof of private health insurance Bring your insurance contract, a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. or proof of expat health insurance If this is your first residence permit, expat health insurance is usually accepted. If you renew your freelance visa, or change an existing residence permit, you usually need public or private health insurance. Health insurance card Show both sides of the card. or proof of public health insurance Get a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB V from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. or proof of private health insurance Bring your insurance contract, a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. or proof of expat health insurance If this is your first residence permit, expat health insurance is usually accepted. If you renew your freelance visa, or change an existing residence permit, you usually need public or private health insurance. Proof of housing You need a place to live where you can register your address. If you apply in Berlin, your home address must be in Berlin. Lease Bring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child). You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, a WG, a sublet or a student residence. and tenancy confirmation ( Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. You might not get a freelance visa without it. Bring it even if you registered your address. and registration certificate ( Anmeldebestätigung) You must register your address to get this document. If you don’t have it, your lease and tenancy confirmation are sometimes enough. At least bring proof that you have a Bürgeramt appointment. and proof of rent payments You must show what you really pay for housing. Print recent bank statements that show rent payments. Lease Bring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child). You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, a WG, a sublet or a student residence. and tenancy confirmation ( Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. You might not get a freelance visa without it. Bring it even if you registered your address. and registration certificate ( Anmeldebestätigung) You must register your address to get this document. If you don’t have it, your lease and tenancy confirmation are sometimes enough. At least bring proof that you have a Bürgeramt appointment. and proof of rent payments You must show what you really pay for housing. Print recent bank statements that show rent payments. Bank statements It shows how much savings you have. In Berlin, € 3,000 to € 5,000 in savings is usually enough. In other cities, you might need around € 10,000. You don’t need a blocked account. If you can, use a German bank. If it’s in another currency, convert it to euros. Translations If your documents are not in German, bring translations. For certificates and official documents, bring certified translations. They sometimes accept untranslated documents, but don’t take the risk. Get translations from Red Tape Translation or Lingoking. If you are over 45 years old, and you are not a citizen of the Dominican Republic, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines or Sri Lanka, you must have… [Berlin.de, Berlin.de, § 21 Abs. 2 and 3 AufenthG, VAB 21.2] Proof of retirement pension Prove that you will get a public or private pension when you are 67 years old.

title: Required documents for a Freiberufler
text: Revenue forecast ( Ertragsvorschau) Make a spreadsheet of your expected monthly business income and expenses. Use the official template. Your numbers must be realistic, but ambitious. At least 2 letters of intent ( Absichtserklärung) These are letters from potential clients that want to hire you. They are very important. They prove that you will find clients and make money. They must show what work you will do, and how much you will get paid. Signed contracts are even better. If you are Selbständig, you need at least 2 letters from clients in Germany. If you are Freiberufler, you don’t need German clients. [§ 21 Abs. 1 AufenthG, § 21 Abs. 5 AufenthG, Berlin.de, Sebastian Hoffmann (August 2023), Sebastian Hoffmann (December 2022), Sebastian Hoffmann (January 2023), exception (2023), exception (2021), Mirko Vorreuter (October 2025)] If you are an artist or a language teacher, you can also bring… Proof of financial support If you can’t prove that you will make enough money, bring proof of financial support. For example… A blocked account Your own savings Regular bank transfers from your family A letter from a guarantor ( Verpflichtungserklärung) A blocked account Your own savings Regular bank transfers from your family A letter from a guarantor ( Verpflichtungserklärung) If you need a permit to do your job (lawyers, doctors, engineers), you must also bring… Occupation practice permit ( Berufsausübungserlaubnis) You must have all the permits and special qualifications needed for the job. For example, doctors, engineers and lawyers need special qualifications. – Find the requirements for your job

title: Required documents for a Selbständiger
text: Business plan This document is a roadmap for your business. It explains your goals, your strategy, your products and your customers. It must show that there is a local interest for your products and services. Learn how to prepare a business plan. Your business plan should include: Company profile ( Firmenprofil) Business concept ( Geschäftskonzept) Company profile ( Firmenprofil) Business concept ( Geschäftskonzept) Financing plan ( Finanzierungsplan) This document details how you plan to finance your business. Use the official template. If you start a business with other people, you must also bring… Shareholder agreement ( Gesellschaftervertrag) If you can, you should also bring… Trade certificate ( Gewerbeschein) Register for trade tax and get your Gewerbeschein. It might be impossible to do this before you get your freelance visa. You can do it later. Trade register entry ( Handelsregisterauszug) You probably don’t need a Handelsregister entry. If you need one, you can probably get it after you get your freelance visa. – Who needs a Handelsregister entry?

title: Required documents at your appointment
text: Appointment confirmation You can’t enter the Ausländerbehörde without it. They check at the door. Have it on your phone or print it. Passport You get your passport back during your appointment; they do not keep it. QR code for biometric pictures (35 × 45 mm) Printed passport photos are not allowed. Only QR codes are accepted. See how to get biometric pictures. Cash, Visa, Mastercard or Girocard You must pay the € 100 application fee. This fee is tax-deductible, so keep the receipt.

title: Optional documents
text: These documents are not required, but some Ausländerbehörde employees ask for them. They make your application more convincing. Letters of recommendation These are letters from your previous employers, clients or professors that recommend you for your work. If you are a scientist or researcher, this is very important. The letters must be related to the work you do. Get 3 or 4 letters if you can. Contracts It proves that you have guaranteed work. Contracts are even better than letters of intent. The contract should explain what you will do, how long you will work and how much you will get paid. Resume or CV Work experience is not required, but it helps. Your resume should prove that you have experience in your field. Don’t include irrelevant experience. Cover letter It explains what you do, and how your business works. It helps the Ausländerbehörde understand what you do. It helps you during your appointment, especially if you don’t speak German. Portfolio or examples of your work It explains what you do, and that you will find clients. If you are an artist, this is very important. For example, you can bring photos of your work, posters of your events, screenshots of your website or apps or newspaper articles about you. You need printed examples; a website address does not work. Proof or education If your education is relevant to your business, prove it. Bring the original diplomas if you can. Copies also work. If you have no relevant education, it’s not a problem.

section: After you get your freelance visa
title: Travel with a freelance visa
text: Your freelance visa lets you visit other Schengen area countries for up to 90 days without a visa. You can travel outside of Germany for up to 6 months. [§ 51 Abs. 1 AufenthG, Berlin.de] If you travel longer, your freelance visa expires. Your freelance visa lets you live anywhere in Germany, not just in the city where you applied. Travel with a residence permit

section: After you get your freelance visa
title: Renew your freelance visa
text: Your freelance visa is valid for up to 3 years. [§ 21 Abs. 4 AufenthG] In Berlin, you must renew it around 6 weeks before it expires, not sooner. How to renew a freelance visa

section: After you get your freelance visa
title: Apply for permanent residence
text: If you have a freelance visa, you qualify for permanent residence after 5 years. If you see “§ 21 Abs. 1” or “§ 21 Abs. 2a” on your freelance visa, you qualify after 3 years. How to apply for permanent residence If you plan to become a permanent resident, start making voluntary public pension payments. You usually need 60 months of pension payments to qualify for permanent residence. The minimum payment is € 111.97 per month. You can also get a private pension instead. Pension requirements for permanent residence
